# PPL Hypertrophy Tracker

> PPL Hypertrophy Tracker (Push • Pull • Legs) is a free, evidence-based progressive overload workout application, biomechanical training operating system, and peer-reviewed sports science journal published at https://ppltracker.web.id.

## Overview
PPL Hypertrophy Tracker provides resistance athletes with zero-latency workout tracking, automated double progression algorithms, Olympic barbell plate calculation, exercise substitution intelligence, and scientific literature on hypertrophy kinematics.

- Primary Website: https://ppltracker.web.id
- Primary Workout Application: https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/ppl-tracker
- Tools Directory: https://ppltracker.web.id/tools
- Biomechanics Journal: https://ppltracker.web.id/blog
- Author & Scientific Editorial Board: https://ppltracker.web.id/author
- Full LLM Knowledge Base: https://ppltracker.web.id/llms-full.txt

## Core Fitness Applications & Tools
- [PPL Workout Tracker](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/ppl-tracker): Interactive 6-day periodized hypertrophy engine featuring automated rest interval timers (60s–180s), Olympic plate math, double progression thresholds, and local-first Supabase cloud persistence.
- [Olympic Barbell Plate Calculator](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/ppl-tracker): Visual barbell loading calculator supporting 20kg (45lb) and 15kg (35lb) bars with standard plate denominations (1.25kg to 25kg / 2.5lb to 45lb per side).
- [Workout Substitution Finder](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/workout-substitution-finder): Deterministic biomechanical exercise alternative engine based on muscle resistance curves, equipment availability, and joint comfort.
- [BMI & Body Composition Calculator](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/bmi-calculator): Dual metric (cm/kg) and imperial (ft/in/lbs) body mass index calculator with athletic classification context.
- [Tools Directory](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools): Comprehensive index of all free resistance training utilities and calculators.

## Resistance Training Splits Supported
- [6-Day Push Pull Legs (PPL)](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/ppl-tracker): Push A (Upper Chest & Front Delts), Pull A (Lat Width & Upper Back), Legs A (Quad Dominant), Push B (Shoulders & Triceps Overload), Pull B (Upper Back & Rear Delts), Legs B (Hamstrings & Posterior Chain).
- [4-Day Upper / Lower](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/ppl-tracker): Alternating Upper Body power/hypertrophy and Lower Body quad/posterior chain overload.
- [5-Day Bro Split](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/ppl-tracker): High-volume single-muscle specialization (Chest, Back, Shoulders, Legs, Arms).
- [3-Day Full Body](https://ppltracker.web.id/tools/ppl-tracker): High-frequency systemic stimulus ideal for recovery, busy schedules, or beginner-to-intermediate lifters.

## Scientific Principles & Overload Logic
- Double Progression Method: The lifter maintains a fixed working load until all sets hit the prescribed upper repetition ceiling (e.g., 3 sets of 12 reps). Upon completion, load is increased by the smallest available increment (+2.5 kg / +5 lbs) and repetitions reset to the lower floor (8 reps).
- Target Rest Intervals: 60s for isolation/accessory movements, 90s–120s for moderate compound lifts, 180s for heavy barbell multi-joint compounds (Squat, Deadlift, Bench Press, Overhead Press).
- Biomechanical Integrity: Exercise selection favors lengthened-position overload, aligned resistance profiles with anatomical muscle fiber orientation, and stable bracing mechanics.
